title: Interventionstudy for ARFID (Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder)
summary:
This study is a follow-up to the first ExpeditionEssen project (DRKS00034963). Its aim is to examine the feasibility, acceptance, and proof of concept of the ExpeditionEssen intervention using a larger sample. The intervention was developed for children with avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) and their caregivers.
The twelve-week online therapy was revised based on initial results and feedback from participants. The basic format remained the same: ExpeditionEssen consists of self-study modules and live video sessions with a therapist.
Participants first complete an online screening. If ARFID is suspected, a diagnostic interview is conducted via video call to verify the primary diagnosis. After inclusion in the study, caregivers are given access to the online platform and self-study modules. In addition, the child and at least one caregiver participate in five video sessions together. The fifth session was added based on participant feedback and replaces a self-study module that was previously in place. 
After completion of the intervention, participants will be asked to fill out questionnaires again, and the diagnostic interview will be repeated. Four weeks after the end of the intervention, another follow-up survey will be conducted.
We assume that the intervention is feasible, will be accepted by the participants, and will reduce the symptoms of avoidant/restrictive eating disorder in the children.

interventions.name: Digital Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, 12 weekly sessions (7 self-guided modules, 5 videotherapy sessions)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
a primary diagnosis of ARFID with a presentation of sensory sensitivity
Exclusion criteria:
severe underweight (<3rd percentile) or tube feeding
Medical conditions contraindicating current treatment
concurrent psychotherapy, dietetic/nutritional counseling, or occupational therapy related to eating behavior
Changes in psychopharmacologic treatment in the past two months, comorbidities interfering with the intervention (e.g., psychotic disorders), or acute suicidality or substance abuse
